why: Reader/actor separation (captain 2026-11-09 19:38Z, hydra#1872). The support agent emits one of these typed intents; a deterministic gate checks the customer's own message, the live record and this policy, and the named actor below performs the write. The agent itself never holds the write tool. Editing this file is the only way to permit an action: there is no prompt, message or tool-arg that can. Markers are ACTION-SPECIFIC and carry the OBJECT of their own intent (a bare 'yes' is refused as policy_invalid generic_marker, a bare 'cancel', 'unsubscribe' or 'address' as broad_marker: 'please unsubscribe me from your newsletter' must never satisfy cancel_subscription, 'please cancel my order' must never satisfy cancel_subscription), a negation in the requesting sentence refuses the intent, a later reversal in the same message refuses it, a request for instructions about the action is not a request for it, and every params_bound value must appear verbatim in the customer's own requesting sentence (QA #1873 r1-r4). The cost is that 'yes, cancel it' alone is refused: Caroline must ask the customer to name the thing ('reply: cancel my subscription').

confirmation_markers: keep my plan with the offer

order_address_update.disabled_why: a free-text address cannot be bound from a chat sentence: the model-supplied value can swallow the customer's withdrawal (QA #1873 r11). Stays off until the address comes from a structured source (a form, or the account's saved address) and the row has a closed params_shape; enabling it is a captain decision.
